scope: compare the third-party 1604220 lobby implementation with our own 1649370 LSG responder

third_party_1604220_lobby.client_answer: 153-byte frame whose last 8 bytes carry CHAL[0:8]
third_party_1604220_lobby.key_derivation: A20 = SHA1(transcript); K = HMAC-SHA1(A20, session_key24); keys = HKDF(K,'BDDATA',72) -> T1|T2|aes_send|aes_recv; CHAL = HKDF(K,'CLIENTCHAL',16)
third_party_1604220_lobby.driving_model: an action script named dw_v3_conn2: hs3[:tail], step1w, evt4, innerNN, redir[:ip:port], ka[:sec], hold[:sec]
third_party_1604220_lobby.task_services_answered: 10 storage | 12/6 title time | 80 marketplace | 102 chat | else empty reply

our_1649370_lsg.dual_build_support: manifest.py explicitly supports 1649370 (original target) and 1604220 (current work target)
our_1649370_lsg.key_method: lsg_crypto.py says the transcript layout is the 1604220 candidate qualified by two independent 1649370 captures; lsg_derived.py replays the derivation against three target-build raw captures
our_1649370_lsg.known_limit: lsg.py states LsgServer is retained only for --legacy-probe; its responses were diagnostic experiments and did not establish a usable lobby

differences_that_matter: theirs uses an explicit action script to sequence replies; ours recomputes keys per capture and answers by service id - the script model is easier to extend and to log

theirs documents HKDF-style key expansion (BDDATA/CLIENTCHAL) while our lsg_crypto uses the calcHmacs variant qualified on 1649370 captures; both need to be checked against a 3.19.26.22 capture before trusting either
theirs answers service 12/6 with a title-time value; our lsg_derived leaves unknown requests unanswered by design
what_we_can_adopt: the action-script idea: make the lobby reply sequence data-driven and log every step with a timestamp so scene transitions can be correlated
the FrameReader zero-control handling from transport.py (a zero-length frame after handshake is a control, not EOF)
their service table (7/10/11/12/23/28/48/71/80/102) as a checklist of what a 3.19 client may ask for
caveat: 1604220 (3.19.26.17) != 1649370 (3.19.26.22); payload bytes and some service answers must be revalidated against our client, and nothing here is evidence that scene=6 works for 1649370
next: add an optional action-script mode to server319 that logs each step, without changing existing verified replies
capture a 3.19.26.22 lobby session and diff its frames against both the 1604220 script and our current answers
keep waiting for the user's version mapping before choosing which implementation becomes the baseline
